bundle.text:
# Chat preset: an API-backed chat mode whose model can only reason, use the
# web tools, and load local skill instructions. Shells, editing, task tools,
# and workspace file tools are out.
- insert:
    - id: preset-chat
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
      config:
        id: chat
        name: Chat
        description: Web chat with search, fetch, reasoning, and skill loading. No shell, edits, or workspace file tools.
        order: 5
        plugins:
          - id: persona
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
            config:
              prefix: |-
                You are a helpful AI assistant. Give accurate, clear, and direct answers.

                You can search the web with web_search and read a specific page with web_fetch. Use them when the question needs current or external information, and cite the source URLs you rely on. If a search fails or a page cannot be fetched, say so and answer from what you know, marking uncertainty.

                Reason carefully before answering, especially for complex or multi-step questions. Do not claim to have read files, run commands, or accessed anything outside this conversation, the web tools, and any skill instructions you load.
              complete: true
              includeRuntimeContext: false
          - id: web-only
            name: '@local/dsh-chat-preset/guard'
          - id: agent-instructions
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
            config:
              maxBytes: 65536
          # Local skill discovery and the `skill` catalog/loader, so chat mode
          # can follow user-level skills such as ub-mode. Discovery alone does
          # not grant file or shell tools; the web-only guard below decides
          # which of these tools stay visible.
          - id: skill-filesystem
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
          - id: tool-skill
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
          - id: tool-web
            name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
            config:
              search: true
              fetch: true
              searchTimeoutMs: 60000
          - id: compaction
            name: cordis:group
            group: true
            isolate:
              compaction: true
            config:
              - id: compaction-basic
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
              - id: command-compact
                name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'

readme.text: A DeepSeek Harness bundle that registers a `chat` agent preset: a plain helpful assistant with web access and local skills, and no way to touch the filesystem or run a command.

The harness composes behaviour from bundles, presets, and plugins. This bundle adds one preset row and one guard plugin, so a session can be switched to a chat mode whose model can search, fetch, and load skill instructions, and nothing else. A preset-scope tool restriction would also filter the preset's own tools, so the restriction is applied per agent once that agent exists.

One preset, mounted from [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `chat` |
| `name` | Chat |
| `order` | 5 |
| persona | helpful assistant, cites sources, marks uncertainty, never claims to have run something it did not |
| tools | `web_search`, `web_fetch`, `skill` |
| compaction | basic compaction plus `/compact` |
The persona is `complete: true`, so it replaces rather than extends the host prompt, and `includeRuntimeContext` is off: chat mode does not get the workspace facts injected.

readme.section: Why a guard instead of a config flag
readme.text: The preset's own tools are registered in the shared preset scope, and the host also registers a few global tools such as `working_directory`. A restriction applied at the preset scope would filter the preset's own tools too, and would miss the globals. So the restriction is applied per agent, once the agent exists.

readme.section: Why a guard instead of a config flag
readme.text: [`lib/guard.js`](lib/guard.js) listens for `agent/created`, reads the tools that agent can actually see, keeps `web_search` and `web_fetch`, adds `skill` when it is present, and calls `agent.ctx.tools.restrict({ allow })`.

readme.section: Why a guard instead of a config flag
readme.text: Reading the allow list from the visible tools rather than hard-coding it means a search-only or fetch-only web configuration still produces the right restriction instead of an empty one. If no web tool is registered at all, the guard logs a warning and leaves the inherited tools unrestricted, which is a deliberate failure mode: it prefers a visible configuration error over silently removing a tool the user asked for.

`skill` reads only the skill files that the discovery provider exposes. It never resolves a workspace path, so keeping it does not widen filesystem access. Dropping it would make user-level skills unreachable in the one mode that most needs them.

```sh
DSH_HOME=${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}
git clone https://github.com/ThomasTZh/dsh-chat-preset \
  "$DSH_HOME/local-plugins/dsh-chat-preset"
```

Register it in `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/package.json` as a dependency:

```json
"@local/dsh-chat-preset": "link:<absolute path to $DSH_HOME>/local-plugins/dsh-chat-preset"
```

and list `@local/dsh-chat-preset` in `dsh.profile.bundles`, then:

```sh
cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" && pnpm install
```
`dsh plugin --profile web add "<path-to-this-clone>"` performs the same registration through the harness CLI.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | `node --test test/guard.test.mjs` | pass, 6 tests |
| Module parses | `node --check lib/guard.js` | pass |
| Install layout | clone into a temporary `DSH_HOME`, then check the package and its patch arrive | pass; `pnpm install` and a harness restart were not run |
**Not tested:** a full preset switch in a freshly installed harness. The machine this bundle was written on runs the preset, but no separate live check was repeated from this repository.

- The guard restricts tools, not prompts. A chat session can still load any skill the discovery provider exposes, by design.
- The preset rows name shipped harness packages (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset`, `dsh-persona`, `dsh-agent-instructions`, and the skill and compaction plugins). They are resolved from the harness install and are not vendored here.
